newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec to sell separation during Canada trade tour.
newsitem.headline: Quebec to sell separation during Canada trade tour.

text.p: The Quebec government said on Thursday that it would promote the separation of the French-speaking province during an upcoming trade mission to Asia led by Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien.

Quebec Deputy Premier Bernard Landry told reporters that Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard would not hestitate to use the economic mission to advance the Parti Quebecois government's separatist policies.

"Quebec sovereignty is a national and an international issue. It is the duty of the Quebec Prime Minister, especially if he is from the Parti Quebecois, to talk to other nations and tell people the truth about what we have in mind," Landry said.
Landry, who is also Quebec's finance minister, said that even though he is Canadian Prime Minister, Chretien does not represent the province's 7.3 million inhabitants.

"It's more complicated than that. There is a federal government there (in Ottawa) and a national government here (in Quebec City). The word national must not be applied to what is federal. The word national is here in the National Assembly (Quebec's legislature)," Landry said.

Earlier on Thursday morning, the Quebec premier's office confirmed that Bouchard will participate in the 12-day tour of the Philippines, South Korea and Thailand as part of the group of provincial premiers dubbed "Team Canada."
Quebec refused to join two earlier federal government-led economic missions to China and India. -- Reuters Montreal bureau (514) 985-2434
